observations: Torah #232 is a one-sentence teaching with no bechina (parallel-aspect) language anywhere in the text. The Rebbe makes a single logical point: when a person recites Pesukei DeZimra (the Psalms of Praise preceding the morning prayer), he is effectively commanding all the angels and all the worlds to praise God — and from this awareness, he should be motivated to pray with genuine kavvanah (heartfelt intention). This is a purely eitza structure: [awareness of prayer's scope] → [arousal to kavvanah]. There are no pairs of concepts that are described as being the same essential thing. Specifically: (1) תפלה (prayer) and הלל/שבח (praise) are not equated — prayer is the vehicle, praise is its content; (2) מלאכים (angels) and עולמות (worlds) are not equated — they are both recipients of the person's command, listed in parallel, but not declared to be bechinot of each other; (3) כוונת הלב (kavvanah) is presented as the desired outcome/conclusion, not as an aspect-equivalent of anything else. The test for a new package is 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain. Torah #232 has 0 such connections. A new package cannot be formed from a text with no bechina statements.
